summary: P. S. Subrahmanya Sastri specialized in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Madras (~1925–1930) and under traditional teachers Nilakantha and Vaidyanatha. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at Annamalai University (~1932–1942).
Padmanabh S. Jaini was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He held posts as professor at the University of California (~1972–1985) and the University of California, Berkeley (~1972–2002).

Palmira Brummett worked in the field of history and archaeology. She studied at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign and the University of Chicago (~1982–1988), and held a post at the University of Tennessee (~1989–2011).
Palmo Kyi works in the field of Tibetology. She studied under supervisor Per Kvaerne (~2008–2012) and teachers Hanna Havnevik and Rinzin Thargyal.

Pamela D. Winfield works in religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. She held a post at Temple University (~2002–2007) and served as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Elon University (~2007).

Indologist Pandurang Vaman Kane studied at the University of Mumbai (~1899–1908). He held positions at Elphinstone High School, Elphinstone College, Wilson College, and the University of Mumbai, later serving as National Professor of Indology (~1959–1972).

Parimal G. Patil specializes in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Harvard University (~1990–1994) and the University of Chicago (~1994–2002), and held a post at Harvard University (~2001).

Parul Dave-Mukherji works in Indology, philosophy, and history and archaeology. She completed a DPhil at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson (1988–1991) and became a professor at Jawaharlal Nehru University (~2006).

Pasang Wangdu is a Tibetology and history and archaeology scholar who studied under the supervision of Anne-Marie Blondeau, Luciano Petech, and Ernst Steinkellner. He held a post as Professor at the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences.

Pascale Haag specializes in Indology and linguistics. She studied under Pierre-Sylvain Filliozat, at Sorbonne Nouvelle University (~1996–2002), and at Paris Nanterre University (-2018), and held a post at EHESS (~2004).

Pascale Hugon works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. She held posts at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (~2006) and the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia (2016).

Pataraporn Sirikanchana is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. She earned a Ph.D. at the University of Pennsylvania (~1981–1985) and became a Professor at Thammasat University (~1985).

Patrice Ladwig works in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Münster, University of Edinburgh, and EHESS, and held posts at the Max Planck Institute for Social Anthropology and the University of Bristol.

Patricia Berger worked in Tibetology, sinology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her Ph.D. at UC Berkeley (~-1980), was Curator of Chinese Art at the Asian Art Museum of San Francisco (~1982–1994), and joined UC Berkeley's faculty in 1996.

Patricia Buckley Ebrey specializes in sinology and history/archaeology. She studied at the University of Chicago (1968) and Columbia University (1970), later holding posts at UIUC (1985), the University of Washington (1997), and IAS (1998).

Patricia Fister works in Japanology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She earned a Ph.D. from the University of Kansas (~-1983), taught there (~1985–1990), and was a professor at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (~1991–2019).

Patricia Schiaffini-Vedani is a sinology and Tibetology scholar. She studied at Peking University (1990–1994) under Zumo Zhou, Zhuhong Zhang, and Shufen Mu, and completed her PhD at the University of Pennsylvania (~-2002) under Perry Link.

Patrick Jory works in history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Western Australia (~-1988) and earned a PhD at Australian National University under Craig J. Reynolds (~1991–1996), taking a post at the University of Queensland (~2009).

Patrick McAllister specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He completed his doctoral studies at the University of Vienna (~2005–2011) under supervisor Helmut Krasser and teachers Karin Preisendanz and Ernst Steinkellner.

Indologist Patrick Olivelle studied at Oxford under Richard Gombrich and Thomas Burrow (~1968–1972) and at Penn under Ludo Rocher (~1972–1974). He held chairmanships at Indiana University (~1984–1991) and the University of Texas at Austin (1991).
